chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Bashar ibn Yasar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:

If you intend something of good, then do not delay it. For a servant fasts on a hot day seeking what is with God, Mighty and Majestic, and God frees him from the Fire; and he gives charity seeking the face of God, and God frees him from the Fire.

key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: charity/alms — voluntary giving in God's path
key_terms.الْخَيْر: good/goodness — any righteous deed or act of obedience
key_terms.الْعَبْد: the servant/worshiper — the human being in relation to God
key_terms.الْيَوْم الْحَارّ: the hot day — fasting in summer heat, a context of significant physical hardship
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — honorific epithet for God
key_terms.مَا عِنْد اللَّه: what is with God — divine reward and nearness in the Hereafter
key_terms.وَجْه اللَّه: the face of God — seeking God's pleasure and approval as the sole motive
key_terms.يُعْتِق: frees/emancipates — liberation from Hell, using the imagery of manumitting a slave

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about not delaying good deeds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) urges the immediate performance of good deeds, warning against procrastination. He illustrates this with two vivid examples — fasting on a scorching day and giving charity — both done purely for God's sake, each resulting in divine liberation from Hellfire. This teaching emphasizes that sincerity of intention combined with prompt action transforms ordinary acts into means of salvation.
